messages:
mila-sales: Rapid prep for tomorrow's call with Oakleaf Credit Union. Ask: strict EU-only processing, BYOK, no cross-border failover even for short DR events, and a signed subprocessor attestation. Need a 60s script + an ops handoff checklist.

rachid-presales: TL;DR: Hosted = strong EU preference but not hard-guaranteed. Dedicated or Private required to meet strict non-failover. BYOK supported on Dedicated/Private after KMS onboarding and policy vetting.

jorge-eng: Hosted detail: traffic is region-preferred; we maintain multi-region fallback for availability which can cross borders. Dedicated: can allocate a single-region reserved pool with a regional-only routing policy and prevent cross-region failover. Private (VPC/on-prem) = full customer control. BYOK flow: key registration -> policy audit -> allowlist + test decrypts.

tess-legal: Subprocessors: EU-located: LogSafe (logging), Observr (metrics), CloudGX (infra), and MirrorDB (replication monitoring). For enterprise we can provide DPA, current subprocessor attestation, SOC2, and a one-off signed attestation workbook. Avoid "never" for Hosted; only promise absolute containment for Dedicated pinned or Private.

mila-sales: Need two conservative lines I can read: one for Hosted and one for Dedicated pinned. Also they asked about egress certificate rotation and proof of chain-of-custody.

jorge-eng: Hosted (safe): "Redwood routes and processes customer workloads primarily in EU regions; in exceptional capacity or recovery events requests may be routed to a compatible region; Redwood will notify customers and provide remediation options."

jorge-eng: Dedicated pinned (safe): "Redwood will provision dedicated capacity in the customer-specified EU region and operate under regional-only routing. Processing and stored customer data will remain in the specified region; only minimal control-plane metadata required for platform health and auditability may be processed outside the region."

tess-legal: Add sentence: "Customer may request the current subprocessor list and a signed attestation workbook; Redwood will furnish standard compliance artifacts on request."

frank-pricing: Ballpark numbers for procurement: one-time onboarding & infra ~$42k, committed monthly for a 2x A100 reserved pool ~$19k/month, BYOK integration & signed attestation workbook ~$6k/year. Final depends on throughput, retention, and SLA terms.

niamh-ops: KMS onboarding timeline: typical 7-21 business days for key exchange, policy checks, and test decrypts. If they require out-of-band attestation or an air-gapped Private deployment add 4-8 weeks. Egress cert rotation: we can share cert fingerprints and rotation cadence; we can allow customer to validate chain-of-custody during onboarding.

niamh-ops: Ops handoff checklist (ticket PROJ-45577): 1) Confirm exact EU region (eu-west1/eu-central1) and any within-jurisdiction standby rules 2) Confirm BYOK key IDs, rotation policy, and KMS endpoint allowlist CIDRs 3) Request signed subprocessor attestation workbook + DPA 4) Define egress certificate delivery & rotation cadence + chain-of-custody proof 5) Agree audit log export cadence and retention 6) Define SLA failure modes and contractual remedies. I'll create PROJ-45577.

mila-sales: Also they asked to see a small config snippet demonstrating regional-only pinning. Can you show something concrete?

jorge-eng: Sample routing policy (Dedicated pinned, strict mode):

```
{"policy_version":"1","routing":{"mode":"strict_pin","primary_region":"eu-central1","standby_within_jurisdiction":false,"fallback":"disabled"}}
```

jorge-eng: Note: "standby_within_jurisdiction" false here means no automatic cross-border or even cross-country standby; for workloads needing hot-standby we can provision warm-edge in same jurisdiction as a separate contract item.

resilience-bot: ticket PROJ-45577 created and assigned to @niamh-ops.

mila-sales: Perfect. I'll use the three lines (Hosted, Dedicated, ops checklist + pricing) on the call and post any customer redlines. Thanks all :thumbsup:
